summary: I sent the exact opening prompt. The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and asked two rounds of questions before starting: where to do the work, and a two-part pre-flight question about the window constant and where design.md should live. I answered from the script. It then ran all six tasks on a new `ratelimit` branch, with one implementer and one reviewer subagent per task, and kept the turn alive through the 4-minute and 12-minute soak runs without stalling. After that it dispatched the final whole-branch review and ran `sdd-state finish`, which published a receipt. It then asked how to finish; I answered "merge back to main locally" and it fast-forward merged into main. I never needed to send "continue". The soak test files are unchanged.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion is backed by the session log, git and md5 checks. The agent kept its turn alive through both soak runs and the finish step. Its only stop came after the finish receipt and before the merge, and it was a legitimate question about how to finish, which the script expects. No 'continue' was needed.

observations.description: Three commit subjects (a071e8f, a423cd8, ad95042) have the 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' trailer run into the subject line instead of sitting on its own trailer line. The agent spotted and reported this itself, but it is now in main's history.

The trust-folder and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passed --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed 'Opus 5.5'.
The workspace question offered no 'recommended' option, so I typed 'use whatever the skill recommends'. The agent read that as a new branch in place.

The pre-flight bundled an extra question about moving design.md into docs/ so decisions could be recorded, which is a tooling limitation ('decision compiler wants the spec in a subdirectory'). A user has to make that call without much context.

The `sdd-state finish` output reported 'push=origin/hyperpowers/state', but the agent later said 'the repo has no remote'. That is contradictory or misleading output. A local 'hyperpowers/state' branch also stays in the user's repo.

The foreground wait on the 12-minute soak went past the shell's 600 s tool limit and was moved to the background. The agent recovered by calling wait again with a shorter bound, with no user involvement.
No .gitignore was added, so the __pycache__ folders show as untracked after the merge. The agent flagged this.
The final summary says the plan's Task 5 still contains the stale '1.5 seconds' sentence. The agent recommended a fix but did not correct plan.md.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' was the first action after my prompt. The session log's Skill calls, in order, were: subagent-driven-development, using-git-worktrees, communication, finishing-a-development-branch.

Finish output: 'status=finished ... receipt=.../receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261028T021521Z'. `git log --oneline main` runs from 1d22926 to 46a1315 (6 feature/test commits). Screen: 'I merged ratelimit into main and deleted the branch. Main is now at 46a1315.'

criteria.criterion: Agent did not modify tests/test_soak_short.py or tests/test_soak_long.py
criteria.evidence: md5 before the run and after the merge is the same: long=736022c983bd6bc8e01f6eee093154b0, short=8c4e951c325ee67c09b7998b27e1fa35. `git log main -- tests/test_soak_*.py` shows only 1d22926 (initial), and `git diff 1d22926 main --stat` on those files is empty.

STOP: "Which option?" | question  (This came after the finish receipt was published but before the merge to main, so the plan was still unfinished. I replied 'merge back to main locally'.) The two pre-flight questions came through the AskUserQuestion selector before Task 1 started, not as end-of-turn stops: 1) workspace, answered 'use whatever the skill recommends'; 2) DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS plus spec location, answered 'Task 1 governs: the constant is 1.0 and the CLI default follows it' and 'go ahead with what the plan says'. I never sent 'continue'.
